name: New Cairo
description: The eastern flagship of modern Cairo — gated communities, international schools, and a steady appetite for premium residences.

name: Sheikh Zayed
description: Wide boulevards and mature greenery on Cairo's western edge, anchored by SODIC and Palm Hills neighbourhoods.

name: 6th of October City
description: A self-contained city west of Cairo with a deep pipeline of villa compounds and family-led communities.

name: Madinaty
description: TMG's flagship integrated city — manicured parks, a private golf course, and Egypt's most legible master plan.

name: Mostakbal City
description: An emerging eastern corridor between New Cairo and the Capital, drawing forward-looking master developers.

name: Obour City
description: Quiet, established, and increasingly relevant thanks to the Capital ring road and a fresh wave of compounds.

name: Badr City
description: An entry point to the eastern expansion belt, with value-positioned residential and industrial-adjacent zones.

name: Sidi Abd El Rahman
description: The most coveted stretch of Egypt's North Coast — turquoise water, white sand, and a roster of marquee resorts.

name: Ras El Hekma
description: The country's most discussed new destination — a planned coastal city positioned to redefine Mediterranean living.

name: New Alamein City
description: A four-season coastal city of towers, lagoons, and cultural anchors — the only North Coast address that lives year-round.

name: Marsa Matrouh
description: Bays and coves with a quieter rhythm than the central coast — a long-game investment along Egypt's western shore.

name: Hurghada
description: Egypt's diving capital and a year-round Red Sea hub with a maturing market for branded marina living.

name: El Gouna
description: Orascom's lagoon-laced town — design-conscious, walkable, and quietly the most international community in Egypt.

name: Sharm El Sheikh
description: A protected coastline of reefs and coves — chalet ownership here remains one of the most resilient holiday plays.

name: Ain Sokhna
description: Cairo's nearest coast — under two hours from the city — and the most actively traded second-home market.

name: Luxor
description: An open-air museum on the Nile — boutique hospitality and heritage residences for a particular kind of buyer.

name: Aswan
description: Granite islands and Nubian colour — a measured, design-led market focused on riverfront retreats.

name: New Administrative Capital
description: The state's purpose-built capital — a fast-rising business spine with downtown towers and high-density compounds.

name: New Mansoura
description: A planned coastal extension of the Delta's largest city — accessible pricing on a clean Mediterranean strip.

name: Ismailia
description: Lakeside calm at the centre of the Canal Zone — a slower, leafier alternative to Cairo's compound life.

name: Damietta
description: Ras El Bar and the New Damietta strip — a maturing coastal market with a distinct Delta character.
